saints.name: St. Pacificus of San Severino
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Franciscan preacher of the Marches who, struck blind, deaf, and lame, turned his long affliction into a hidden life of prayer…
biography: Carlo Antonio Divini was born at San Severino in the March of Ancona on 1 March 1653, the youngest of thirteen children, and was orphaned of both parents while still a child. In 1670 he took the habit of the Franciscan Reformati at Forano, receiving the name Pacificus, and was ordained a priest on 4 June 1678.

After six years teaching philosophy to the younger friars, he laboured as a missionary preacher among the country people. From 1684 his health failed: he grew lame, then deaf, and at last blind, so that he could preach no more. For the remaining thirty-seven years of his life he bore these afflictions in patience, given to prayer before the Blessed Sacrament and to the counsel of those who sought him.

He was said to have foretold the earthquake that devastated the Abruzzi in 1703, and wonders were reported at his tomb. He died at San Severino on 24 September 1721, was beatified by Pius VI in 1786, and canonized by Gregory XVI in 1839. As one who suffered long infirmity without complaint, he is invoked as the patron of the chronically ill.
saints.knownFor: His patient endurance of affliction and his hidden life of prayer.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), "St. Pacificus of San Severino"
